newsitem.title: MEXICO: Investors bullish on Mexican local rates - Abaco.
newsitem.headline: Investors bullish on Mexican local rates - Abaco.

text.p: Both local and foreign investors are "very bullish" on local interest rates mainly due to the stability of the peso, brokerage house Abaco said in a report written last week and released on Monday.

Mexico's primary interest rates fell last week, for the second straight week, as demand, especially for the 90-day and 180-day paper, far outstripped demand at the central bank's auction of treasury bills, Abaco noted.
Some analysts expect Cetes rates to be unchanged or slightly higher at Banco de Mexico's auction this Tuesday, in response to gains in the U.S. long bond yields and a soft peso.
On Monday, Abaco economist Alexander Anderson told Reuters that events in the financial markets could put a slight upward pressure on rates, but that this would be contained by strong demand.
"The demand for Mexican government securities is extremely strong," he said.

A recent announcement by Banco de Mexico that it will sell dollars if the peso depreciates sharply has convinced local money market traders that rate hikes will not be as violent as in the past two years, Anderson said in the report.
"This has encouraged them to take longer positions in Cetes," he wrote.
As well, the drop in inflation, which was only 0.66 percent of the first half of March, has also influenced rates.
"If inflation for March is 1.3 percent, this means that the 28-day Cete, at 20.59 percent, is now positive in real terms," he said. "We expect inflation to be 1.1 percent for April."
Mexico's rates fell last week while the U.S. federal funds rate rose.

"This, combined with a slight appreciation of the Mexican currency, points to the enormous stability which now exists in Mexican financial markets, which seem to easily absorb exogenous shocks," Anderson said.
